title: Myriad Genetics works with AWS to make AI for faster document handling
excerpt: Myriad Genetics partners with AWS to enhance Image Genius, speeding up document processing, and improving insurance workflows for diagnostics.
content_html:
Myriad Genetics processes an estimated 1.5 million diagnostic tests annually, including screening for hereditary cancer and prenatal conditions, tumor profiling, and assessments of how genes may affect the body's response to mental health medications.

It can take months for the Salt Lake City-based molecular diagnostic testing company to process all the paperwork necessary to get paid, a process known as revenue cycle management, which requires health organizations like Myriad to dedicate staff to software, medical coding, and regulatory compliance to manage billing for medical services.

To speed up document processing, Myriad internally developed an AI tool to automate the company's diagnostic, insurance, and reimbursement operations. After launching a version of that tool in 2024 that proved too costly to maintain, Myriad brought in cloud computing giant Amazon Web Services to lower the project's ongoing costs.

With new artificial intelligence capabilities, Myriad's end-to-end document processing has decreased from an average of 10 minutes to 20 seconds per document. This is helping to accelerate repayment cycles, said Martyna Shallenberg, Myriad's senior director of software engineering.

"The sooner we get cash, the better," Shallenberg told Business Insider. She said that typically, it can take up to 18 months for companies like Myriad to receive full reimbursement for a testing order because of the complexities of processing insurance claims.

Shallenberg — along with the Myriad's chief technology officer, his predecessor, and an expert at AWS — spoke with Business Insider about the evolution of the project over nearly three years.

The tech

In the fourth quarter of 2023, Myriad conceptualized a tool that could use AI to classify pathology reports, automate document tagging, and extract Medicare keywords, Kevin Haas, Myriad's former CTO, told Business Insider in a March interview.

A week after speaking with Business Insider, Haas — who worked at Myriad for eight years and spent five years in the CTO role — departed to become chief development and technology officer at cancer diagnostics company Veracyte.

Haas said he wanted to use AI to speed up prior authorization, a process where a doctor secures approval from an insurance provider before ordering one of Myriad's tests for their patient. Once a doctor made this request, an authorization specialist had to sort through the thousands of health plans and insurance payers that handle these claims.

Myriad also needs to act quickly. Once a sample is collected by a doctor, prior authorization is often required within days, or even hours, to secure health insurance coverage for patients, said Shallenberg. If prior authorization for the diagnostic tests isn't obtained, an insurer could deny the claim, potentially delaying patient care or resulting in a loss of revenue for Myriad, she added.

In the second quarter of 2024, Haas and Myriad worked with consulting giant PwC to build the first version of its intelligent document processing tool, called Image Genius, which used machine learning service Amazon Textract and natural language processing service Amazon Comprehend to automate document classification, extract data from pathology reports, process insurance cards, and reduce manual document handling, said Shallenberg.

Myriad rolled out Image Genius for its hereditary cancer business in the third quarter of 2024, to automate medical document classification and streamline revenue cycle workflows, a Myriad spokesperson told Business Insider.

A cost- and data-conscious pivot

In the fourth quarter of 2024, as Myriad planned to expand Image Genius to additional business units, it ran into some issues around costs, longer-than-expected processing times, and difficulty extracting the right clinical information from dense pathology reports, said Haas.

Haas said Myriad determined that the internally developed AI tool needed constant maintenance and upgrading. "The inputs are as vast as the millions of samples we get every year," Haas said.

Myriad also discovered that the AI system wasn't always astute enough to differentiate a testing order from a doctor's medical notes, said Shallenberg. "It was actually the hardest part of the process, separating those documents," she added.

Shallenberg said that Myriad spent the first quarter of 2025 refining the AI model's prompts to improve the accuracy of its outputs. They also provided more data samples to give the system greater context, but decided results from this current iteration of Image Genius weren't worth the cost, said Shallenberg. AWS Comprehend, which uses machine learning to identify clinical notes, pathology reports, insurance information, and other data from unstructured text and data, was "very expensive," she said.

Myriad pivoted that same quarter to begin working with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center, a team of scientists and AI experts that helps customers steer AI projects from conception to full rollout.

By the spring of 2025, AWS and Myriad rebuilt Image Genius on Amazon Bedrock, which allows companies to access foundational models from vendors like Anthropic and OpenAI, and Amazon Nova, the tech giant's family of AI models, Dr. Rowland Illing, AWS' global chief medical officer, told Business Insider.

Illing said this architecture allowed Myriad to tinker with various models and pick the best model based on speed, accuracy, and cost. "Model choice is really important," he said.

The outcome

By the third quarter of 2025, AWS and Myriad completed the engineering work needed to develop the next-generation platform. Image Genius officially relaunched in the first quarter of 2026.

A Myriad spokesperson said the new Image Genius tool has saved staff an estimated 300 hours a month across about 9,000 prior authorizations in the women's health division. The tool will roll out next to the oncology and mental health units sometime in 2027, the Myriad spokesperson added.

Image Genius is being spearheaded by Myriad's new CTO, Raj Jampa, who joined the company in June 2026 after previously holding senior technology leadership roles at Agilent Technologies, Exact Sciences, and Genomic Health.

Jampa told Business Insider that his goal was to work with Myriad CEO Sam Raha and other senior leaders to ramp up AI use and automation across all aspects of the revenue cycle, including eligibility verification, claims submission, denial management, and appeals handling.

John Kell is a New York-based freelance writer, covering a wide range of topics from beverages to technology to DEI and sustainability. He is particularly interested in how leaders and the business community are responding to changes in culture and how they position their businesses for growth in a fast-changing world.  John previously worked as an on-staff reporter for Fortune Magazine, The Wall Street Journal, and Dow Jones Newswires, covering food and beverage, retailers, restaurants, and apparel makers. He received a bachelor's degree in journalism from The College of New Jersey.

content_html_zh:
Myriad Genetics 每年估计进行 150 万次诊断测试，包括遗传性癌症和产前疾病筛查、肿瘤分析以及基因如何影响身体对心理健康药物反应的评估。

这家位于盐湖城的分子诊断测试公司可能需要几个月的时间才能处理获得报酬所需的所有文书工作，这一过程被称为收入周期管理，它要求 Myriad 等健康组织专门配备员工从事软件、医疗编码和法规遵从性工作，以管理医疗服务的计费。

为了加快文档处理速度，Myriad 内部开发了一款人工智能工具来自动化公司的诊断、保险和报销操作。 在 2024 年推出该工具的一个版本后，事实证明维护成本太高，Myriad 引入了云计算巨头 Amazon Web Services，以降低该项目的持续成本。

凭借新的人工智能功能，Myriad 的端到端文档处理时间已从平均每个文档 10 分钟减少到 20 秒。 Myriad 的软件工程高级总监 Martyna Shallenberg 表示，这有助于加快还款周期。

“我们越早拿到现金越好，”沙伦伯格告诉《商业内幕》。 她表示，由于处理保险索赔的复杂性，像 Myriad 这样的公司通常需要长达 18 个月的时间才能收到测试订单的全额报销。

Shallenberg 与 Myriad 的首席技术官、他的前任以及 AWS 的一位专家一起接受《商业内幕》采访，谈论了该项目近三年来的演变。

技术

Myriad 前首席技术官凯文·哈斯 (Kevin Haas) 在 3 月份的采访中告诉《商业内幕》，2023 年第四季度，Myriad 概念化了一种工具，可以使用人工智能对病理报告进行分类、自动化文档标记和提取医疗保险关键字。

在与《商业内幕》交谈一周后，哈斯——在 Myriad 工作了八年，并担任了五年首席技术官——离职，成为癌症诊断公司 Veracyte 的首席开发和技术官。

Haas 表示，他希望使用人工智能来加快事先授权的速度，在这一过程中，医生在为患者订购 Myriad 的一项检测之前，需要获得保险公司的批准。 一旦医生提出此请求，授权专家就必须对处理这些索赔的数千个健康计划和保险付款人进行分类。

Myriad 也需要迅速采取行动。 沙伦伯格说，一旦医生收集了样本，通常需要在几天甚至几小时内获得事先授权，以确保为患者提供医疗保险。 她补充说，如果未获得诊断测试的事先授权，保险公司可能会拒绝索赔，从而可能会延误患者护理或导致 Myriad 的收入损失。

Shallenberg 表示，2024 年第二季度，Haas 和 Myriad 与咨询巨头普华永道合作构建了其智能文档处理工具的第一个版本，名为 Image Genius，该工具使用机器学习服务 Amazon Textract 和自然语言处理服务 Amazon Comprehend 来自动进行文档分类、从病理报告中提取数据、处理保险卡并减少手动文档处理。

Myriad 发言人告诉 Business Insider，Myriad 于 2024 年第三季度为其遗传性癌症业务推出了 Image Genius，以实现医疗文档分类自动化并简化收入周期工作流程。

注重成本和数据的支点

Haas 表示，2024 年第四季度，Myriad 计划将 Image Genius 扩展到其他业务部门，但遇到了一些问题，包括成本、处理时间长于预期以及难以从密集的病理报告中提取正确的临床信息。

Haas 表示，Myriad 认为内部开发的人工智能工具需要不断维护和升级。 “输入的数据与我们每年获得的数百万个样本一样巨大，”哈斯说。

沙伦伯格说，Myriad 还发现，人工智能系统并不总是足够聪明，无法区分测试订单和医生的医疗记录。 “这实际上是整个过程中最困难的部分，分离这些文件，”她补充道。

Shallenberg 表示，Myriad 在 2025 年第一季度完善了人工智能模型的提示，以提高其输出的准确性。 Shallenberg 表示，他们还提供了更多数据样本，为系统提供更多背景信息，但 Image Genius 当前迭代的结果不值得付出代价。 她说，AWS Comprehend 使用机器学习从非结构化文本和数据中识别临床记录、病理报告、保险信息和其他数据，“非常昂贵”。

Myriad 在同一季度开始与 AWS Generative AI 创新中心合作，该中心是一个由科学家和 AI 专家组成的团队，帮助客户引导 AI 项目从概念到全面部署。

AWS 全球首席医疗官 Rowland Illing 博士告诉 Business Insider，到 2025 年春季，AWS 和 Myriad 在 Amazon Bedrock 上重建了 Image Genius，使公司能够访问来自 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 等供应商的基础模型，以及科技巨头的人工智能模型系列 Amazon Nova。

Illing 表示，这种架构允许 Myriad 修改各种模型，并根据速度、准确性和成本选择最佳模型。 “模型的选择非常重要，”他说。

结果

到 2025 年第三季度，AWS 和 Myriad 完成了开发下一代平台所需的工程工作。 Image Genius 于 2026 年第一季度正式重新推出。

Myriad 发言人表示，新的 Image Genius 工具在女性健康部门的约 9,000 项事先授权中为员工节省了大约 300 个小时的时间。 Myriad 发言人补充说，该工具将于 2027 年的某个时候在肿瘤科和心理健康科旁边推出。

Image Genius 由 Myriad 的新任首席技术官 Raj Jampa 领导，他于 2026 年 6 月加入公司，此前曾在 Agilent Technologies、Exact Sciences 和 Genomic Health 担任高级技术领导职务。

Jampa 告诉 Business Insider，他的目标是与 Myriad 首席执行官 Sam Raha 和其他高级领导人合作，在收入周期的各个方面加强人工智能的使用和自动化，包括资格验证、索赔提交、拒绝管理和上诉处理。

约翰·凯尔 (John Kell) 是一位驻纽约的自由撰稿人，涵盖从饮料到技术再到 DEI 和可持续发展等广泛主题。 他特别感兴趣的是领导者和商界如何应对文化变化，以及他们如何定位自己的业务，以在快速变化的世界中实现增长。 约翰此前曾担任《财富》杂志、《华尔街日报》和道琼斯通讯社的专职记者，报道食品和饮料、零售商、餐馆和服装制造商。 他获得了新泽西学院新闻学学士学位。
